title: Malformed odd-length PCM16 buffers can raise uncaught resampling errors
reasoning: The protocol says chunks are PCM16 mono, but resample_pcm16_mono passes arbitrary bytes directly to np.frombuffer(dtype=np.int16). If a malformed or truncated audio chunk has an odd byte length and needs resampling, NumPy raises ValueError because the buffer size is not a multiple of int16. handle_audio_chunk does not catch or normalize this, so one malformed frame can fail the provider task instead of being rejected predictably.
reproduction: Call resample_pcm16_mono(b'\x00', 16000, 24000) or OpenAIRealtimeTranscriptionSession.handle_audio_chunk with a one-byte buffer and a non-24000 sample rate.
recommendation: Validate that PCM16 input length is even before np.frombuffer. Either raise a clear ValueError at the frame boundary, drop the trailing byte with logging, or reject the frame without tearing down the streaming session.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked audio-frame tests were included, and the helper lacks an explicit edge-case guard for malformed PCM16 byte lengths.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add an audio_frames unit test for odd-length PCM16 input during resampling and assert the chosen behavior is deterministic and does not surface an unhandled NumPy exception.
minimumFixScope: backend/src/api/services/transcription/audio_frames.py input validation plus a focused helper test.
